Subject: Immediate capacity concern — Q4 burst sequencing

David / Laura / Marissa,

We're grateful for Redwood's support so far. Our Q4 product launch has accelerated and we just finalized a vendor integration that will increase steady-state throughput by ~3.6x starting 2028-10-01. That rise pushes us past the committed tranche in our reserved capacity plan for Q4.

We need to lock in a short-term prioritization to avoid customer-facing latency regressions during the launch window. Specifically: can Redwood sequence our committed GPUs into a temporary tranche (2 weeks) to cover launch traffic, or offer burst lanes tied to our commit? We can compensate with credits or a short-term top-up invoice.

I attached our internal commit schedule (saturn_commit_schedule.csv) and a high-level rollout calendar. Clive and I are available this week for a 30-minute alignment call.

Thanks — Olivia

Folks — forwarding Saturn's note. Summary: they request a 2-week tranche for launch (Q4) and are open to credits/top-up. This will intersect with two high-commit deals in the same US-west pool (Deal: ORION-Alpha and Deal: BRIGHTHAR-Reserved).

Prelim thinking (fast triage):
- Option A: create a temporary tranche carved from unallocated headroom and set it as non-preemptible for the 2-week window (costly but safest for Saturn).
- Option B: offer a burst lane (best-effort) with soft SLOs and compensatory credits if we experience queueing.
- Option C: move some lower-priority customers onto alternative model variants (quantized) for the window and free up capacity (operationally more complex).

Please review attached headroom_analysis_Q4.xlsx. Jordan — can you model the delta in committed token throughput if we choose A vs B (ballpark numbers only) and reply with recommended pricing offsets?

We need a recommendation by EOD tomorrow to keep Saturn in our pipeline and avoid a potential escalation.

Laura

On Tue, Feb 14, 2028 at 3:22 PM laura.bennett@redwood.ai wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Saturn's note. Summary: they request a 2-week tranche for launch (Q4) and are open to credits/top-up. This will intersect with two high-commit deals in the same US-west pool (Deal: ORION-Alpha and Deal: BRIGHTHAR-Reserved).

Quick numbers and recommendation:
- Current unallocated headroom (US-west active pool) for Q4 estimated: ~420 GPU-hours/day (see headroom_analysis_Q4.xlsx).
- Saturn peak incremental demand estimated: ~250 GPU-hours/day during the 2-week launch window.
- Option A (non-preemptible tranche): requires carving ~250 GPU-hours/day -> we'd have to negotiate partial shifting of 140 GPU-hours/day from ORION-Alpha (they have flexibility window in mid-Nov) and 60 GPU-hours/day from BRIGHTHAR (they already agreed to some smoothing). Net remaining gap: ~50 GPU-hours/day.
- Option B (burst lane best-effort): no carving required but risk of queueing -> recommend an SLA credit structure: 10% credit if p95 latency > 350ms for > 2 hours in the window.
- Option C (model-variant relocation): ops overhead + customer coordination; lower cost to Redwood but risky for downstream app fidelity.

Recommended path: Hybrid (A + B) — carve the bulk (200 GPU-hours/day) as a short-lived temporary tranche and supplement with a controlled burst lane for residual demand. Commercial: propose 40% discount on added capacity for the 2-week tranche in exchange for a one-time committed extension into Q1 (3 months at a lowered rate) — buy-down to offset lost margin.

I attached a draft temporary_tranche_agreement-draft.pdf with the commercial language. If Laura approves, we can present to Saturn with a one-page mutual action plan and a draft DocuSign.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference

2) Commercials: 40% off for the temporary tranche capacity for the 2-week window, in exchange for a 3-month committed extension of your Dedicated contract into Q1 (same region, modest rate lock). We'll send a draft DocuSign for signature.

- Redwood Ops: scheduling and cutover plan for carving the tranche will follow within 48 hours of signature.
